(`aws_iam_role`) with role-specific inline or attached policies (`aws_iam_role_policy` or `aws_iam_policy` + `aws_iam_role_policy_attachment`).\n\n## Global Least-Privilege Rules\n\n- Never use wildcard actions (`Action = \"*\"` or `service:*`) or wildcard resources (`Resource = \"*\"`) in any `Allow` statement across any role policy.\n- **Per-workload CloudWatch Log Group isolation**: Each logging workload (`ecs_execution`, `ecs_task`, `projector`, `relay`, `archiver`) may only grant CloudWatch Logs write permissions (`logs:CreateLogStream`, `logs:PutLogEvents`, `logs:DescribeLogStreams`) on its **own** dedicated CloudWatch Log Group ARN (`arn:aws:logs:<region>:<account>:log-group:/clearledger/<resource_prefix>/<workload>*`). Do not use a shared `/clearledger/<resource_prefix>/*` or `/clearledger/*` log group wildcard that permits one workload to write into another workload's log group, and do not grant any CloudWatch Logs actions to `scheduler_role_arn`.\n- **Strict KMS key isolation across all six roles**: Each workload may only be granted `kms:Decrypt`, `kms:GenerateDataKey`, and `kms:DescribeKey` on the specific customer-managed KMS keys required for the data stores it accesses at runtime. No role may grant `kms:Decrypt` or `kms:GenerateDataKey` on any of the other KMS keys, and `ecs_execution_role_arn` and `scheduler_role_arn` must not grant access to any of the four KMS keys.\n- **Defense-in-depth explicit `Deny` guardrail statements**: Do not rely solely on implicit omission for forbidden permissions. Every role's policy document must include explicit `Effect = \"Deny\"` statement(s) covering all forbidden actions and resources listed under **Forbidden access (`Effect = \"Deny\"` required)** for that role below.\n- **Out-of-band IAM policy drift reconciliation in `deploy.sh`**: During `deploy.sh`, any out-of-band inline policies (`DeleteRolePolicy`) or attached customer-managed/AWS-managed policies (`DetachRolePolicy`) added to any of the six ClearLedger IAM roles outside Terraform/OpenTofu must be removed so that each role retains only its canonical least-privilege policy, and any detached out-of-band customer-managed IAM policies prefixed with `<resource_prefix>` must also be deleted (`DeletePolicy`, after deleting any non-default policy versions).\n\n## Role Responsibilities and Access Boundaries\n\n1. **`ecs_execution_role_arn`**:\n   - **Trust principal**: `ecs-tasks.amazonaws.com` (and no other service or wildcard principal).\n   - **Allowed access (`Effect = \"Allow\"`)**: CloudWatch Logs stream creation/writing (`logs:CreateLogStream`, `logs:PutLogEvents`, `logs:DescribeLogStreams`) scoped strictly to `logs.api_log_group`.\n   - **Forbidden access (`Effect = \"Deny\"` required)**: Must not allow, and must explicitly deny via `Effect = \"Deny\"`, any SQS actions (`sqs:SendMessage`, `sqs:ReceiveMessage`, `sqs:DeleteMessage`) on the main queue or DLQ, any DynamoDB actions (`dynamodb:GetItem`, `dynamodb:PutItem`, `dynamodb:UpdateItem`, `dynamodb:DeleteItem`, `dynamodb:Query`) on the projection table or `AccountIndex`, any S3 actions (`s3:GetObject`, `s3:PutObject`, `s3:DeleteObject`, `s3:ListBucket`) on the audit bucket (`<audit_bucket_arn>` and `<audit_bucket_arn>/*`), `kms:Decrypt` or `kms:GenerateDataKey` on all four KMS keys (`database`, `messaging`, `projection`, `audit`), and `logs:CreateLogStream` or `logs:PutLogEvents` on the three non-API CloudWatch Log Groups (`projector`, `relay`, `archiver`).\n2. **`ecs_task_role_arn`**:\n   - **Trust principal**: `ecs-tasks.amazonaws.com`.\n   - **Allowed access (`Effect = \"Allow\"`)**:\n     - Publish-only access on the main SQS queue ARN (`sqs:SendMessage`, `sqs:GetQueueAttributes`, `sqs:GetQueueUrl`).\n     - Read-only access on the projection DynamoDB table ARN and its specific `AccountIndex` GSI ARN `<table_arn>/index/AccountIndex` (`dynamodb:GetItem`, `dynamodb:Query`, `dynamodb:DescribeTable`; do not use `<table_arn>/index/*` or `<table_arn>/*` wildcards).\n     - Cryptographic usage (`kms:Decrypt`, `kms:GenerateDataKey`, `kms:DescribeKey`) on the `messaging` and `projection` KMS key ARNs only.\n     - CloudWatch Logs stream creation/writing scoped strictly to `logs.api_log_group`.\n   - **Forbidden access (`Effect = \"Deny\"` required)**: Must not allow, and must explicitly deny via `Effect = \"Deny\"`, consuming or deleting SQS messages (`sqs:ReceiveMessage`, `sqs:DeleteMessage`) on the main queue or `sqs:SendMessage`/`sqs:ReceiveMessage`/`sqs:DeleteMessage` on the DLQ; mutating DynamoDB (`dynamodb:PutItem`, `dynamodb:UpdateItem`, `dynamodb:DeleteItem`, `dynamodb:DeleteTable`) on the projection table; any S3 access (`s3:GetObject`, `s3:PutObject`, `s3:DeleteObject`, `s3:ListBucket`) on `<audit_bucket_arn>` and `<audit_bucket_arn>/*`; `kms:Decrypt` or `kms:GenerateDataKey` on the `database` and `audit` KMS keys; and `logs:CreateLogStream` or `logs:PutLogEvents` on any non-API log group (`projector`, `relay`, `archiver`). Furthermore, must not grant `dynamodb:Query` on `<table_arn>/index/*`.\n3. **`projector_role_arn`**:\n   - **Trust principal**: `lambda.amazonaws.com`.\n   - **Allowed access (`Effect = \"Allow\"`)**:\n     - Consume-only access on the main SQS queue ARN (`sqs:ReceiveMessage`, `sqs:DeleteMessage`, `sqs:GetQueueAttributes`, `sqs:ChangeMessageVisibility`) and dead-letter forwarding (`sqs:SendMessage`) on the DLQ ARN.\n     - Append/monotonic-upsert access on the projection DynamoDB table ARN and its specific `AccountIndex` GSI ARN `<table_arn>/index/AccountIndex` (`dynamodb:GetItem`, `dynamodb:PutItem`, `dynamodb:UpdateItem`, `dynamodb:Query`; do not use `<table_arn>/index/*` or `<table_arn>/*` wildcards).\n     - Cryptographic usage (`kms:Decrypt`, `kms:GenerateDataKey`, `kms:DescribeKey`) on the `messaging` and `projection` KMS key ARNs only.\n     - CloudWatch Logs stream creation/writing scoped strictly to `logs.projector_log_group`.\n   - **Forbidden access (`Effect = \"Deny\"` required)**: Must not allow, and must explicitly deny via `Effect = \"Deny\"`, `sqs:SendMessage` on the main queue or `sqs:ReceiveMessage`/`sqs:DeleteMessage` on the DLQ; deleting DynamoDB items (`dynamodb:DeleteItem`) or tables (`dynamodb:DeleteTable`) on the projection table; any S3 access (`s3:GetObject`, `s3:PutObject`, `s3:DeleteObject`, `s3:ListBucket`) on `<audit_bucket_arn>` and `<audit_bucket_arn>/*`; `kms:Decrypt` or `kms:GenerateDataKey` on the `database` and `audit` KMS keys; and `logs:CreateLogStream` or `logs:PutLogEvents` on any non-projector log group (`api`, `relay`, `archiver`). Furthermore, must not grant `dynamodb:Query` on `<table_arn>/index/*`.\n4. **`relay_role_arn`**:\n   - **Trust principal**: `lambda.amazonaws.com`.\n   - **Allowed access (`Effect = \"Allow\"`)**:\n     - Publish-only access on the main SQS queue ARN (`sqs:SendMessage`, `sqs:GetQueueAttributes`, `sqs:GetQueueUrl`).\n     - Cryptographic usage (`kms:Decrypt`, `kms:GenerateDataKey`, `kms:DescribeKey`) on the `messaging` and `database` KMS key ARNs only.\n     - CloudWatch Logs stream creation/writing scoped strictly to `logs.relay_log_group`.\n   - **Forbidden access (`Effect = \"Deny\"` required)**: Must not allow, and must explicitly deny via `Effect = \"Deny\"`, `sqs:ReceiveMessage` or `sqs:DeleteMessage` on the main queue, `sqs:SendMessage`/`sqs:ReceiveMessage`/`sqs:DeleteMessage` on the DLQ, any DynamoDB actions (`dynamodb:GetItem`, `dynamodb:PutItem`, `dynamodb:UpdateItem`, `dynamodb:DeleteItem`, `dynamodb:Query`) on the projection table or `AccountIndex`, any S3 actions (`s3:GetObject`, `s3:PutObject`, `s3:DeleteObject`, `s3:ListBucket`) on `<audit_bucket_arn>` and `<audit_bucket_arn>/*`, `kms:Decrypt` or `kms:GenerateDataKey` on the `projection` and `audit` KMS keys, and `logs:CreateLogStream` or `logs:PutLogEvents` on any non-relay log group (`api`, `projector`, `archiver`).\n5. **`archiver_role_arn`**:\n   - **Trust principal**: `lambda.amazonaws.com`.\n   - **Allowed access (`Effect = \"Allow\"`)**:\n     - Append-only object access (`s3:PutObject`, `s3:GetObject`, `s3:AbortMultipartUpload`) scoped strictly to `<audit_bucket_arn>/ledger-audit/*`, and bucket-level metadata (`s3:ListBucket`, `s3:GetBucketLocation`) scoped strictly to `<audit_bucket_arn>` (keep object-level and bucket-level statements separated by resource type).\n     - Cryptographic usage (`kms:Decrypt`, `kms:GenerateDataKey`, `kms:DescribeKey`) on the `audit` and `database` KMS key ARNs only.\n     - CloudWatch Logs stream creation/writing scoped strictly to `logs.archiver_log_group`.\n   - **Forbidden access (`Effect = \"Deny\"` required)**: Must not grant `s3:PutObject` on the bucket ARN `<audit_bucket_arn>` or unscoped `<audit_bucket_arn>/*` root wildcard, and must not grant `s3:ListBucket` on object ARNs. Must explicitly deny via `Effect = \"Deny\"` `s3:DeleteObject` and `s3:DeleteObjectVersion` on `<audit_bucket_arn>` and `<audit_bucket_arn>/*`, any SQS actions (`sqs:SendMessage`, `sqs:ReceiveMessage`, `sqs:DeleteMessage`) on the main queue or DLQ, any DynamoDB actions (`dynamodb:GetItem`, `dynamodb:PutItem`, `dynamodb:UpdateItem`, `dynamodb:DeleteItem`, `dynamodb:Query`) on the projection table or `AccountIndex`, `kms:Decrypt` or `kms:GenerateDataKey` on the `messaging` and `projection` KMS keys, and `logs:CreateLogStream` or `logs:PutLogEvents` on any non-archiver log group (`api`, `projector`, `relay`).\n6. **`scheduler_role_arn`**:\n   - **Trust principal**: `scheduler.amazonaws.com`.\n   - **Allowed access (`Effect = \"Allow\"`)**:\n     - `lambda:InvokeFunction` scoped strictly to the Outbox Relay (`workers.outbox_relay.function_arn`) and Audit Archiver (`workers.audit_archiver.function_arn`) Lambda function ARNs.\n   - **Forbidden access (`Effect = \"Deny\"` required)**: Must not allow, and must explicitly deny via `Effect = \"Deny\"`, `lambda:InvokeFunction` on the Projector Lambda (`workers.projector.function_arn`), any SQS actions (`sqs:SendMessage`, `sqs:ReceiveMessage`, `sqs:DeleteMessage`) on the main queue or DLQ, any DynamoDB actions (`dynamodb:GetItem`, `dynamodb:PutItem`, `dynamodb:UpdateItem`, `dynamodb:DeleteItem`, `dynamodb:Query`) on the projection table or `AccountIndex`, any S3 actions (`s3:GetObject`, `s3:PutObject`, `s3:DeleteObject`, `s3:ListBucket`) on `<audit_bucket_arn>` and `<audit_bucket_arn>/*`, `kms:Decrypt` or `kms:GenerateDataKey` on all four KMS keys (`database`, `messaging`, `projection`, `audit`), and `logs:CreateLogStream` or `logs:PutLogEvents` on all four CloudWatch Log Groups (`api`, `projector`, `relay`, `archiver`).\n=== kms\n# Customer-Managed KMS Keys (`services/kms.md`)\n\nProvision four separate customer-managed KMS keys (`aws_kms_key`) and four KMS aliases (`aws_kms_alias`):\n\n- `kms.database_arn` with alias `alias/<resource_prefix>-database`: encrypts the RDS PostgreSQL instance\n- `kms.messaging_arn` with alias `alias/<resource_prefix>-messaging`: encrypts the main SQS queue and DLQ\n- `kms.projection_arn` with alias `alias/<resource_prefix>-projection`: encrypts the DynamoDB projection table\n- `kms.audit_arn` with alias `alias/<resource_prefix>-audit`: encrypts the S3 audit archive bucket\n\nEach of the four KMS keys must be configured with:\n- `enable_key_rotation = true`\n- `deletion_window_in_days = 10` (must be `10..30` days)\n- Tag `ClearLedgerDeployment = <resource_prefix>`\n\n=== cloudwatch-logs\n# CloudWatch Log Groups (`services/cloudwatch-logs.md`)\n\nProvision The control plane is AWS SDK / CLI / Terraform compatible, and HTTP listeners can forward to registered instance targets using the target's reachable local address.\n\n> Classic (v1) Elastic Load Balancing is a **different API** served from the same endpoint host —\n> see [ELB Classic (v1)](elb-classic.md). Requests are routed by their `Version` parameter:\n> `2015-12-01` here, `2012-06-01` there.\n\n## Supported Actions\n\n### Load Balancers\n\n| Action | Description |\n|--------|-------------|\n| CreateLoadBalancer | Creates an ALB or NLB in active state with persisted attributes and tags. |\n| DescribeLoadBalancers | Lists or returns stored load balancers. |\n| DeleteLoadBalancer | Deletes a load balancer and stops its listener sockets. |\n| ModifyLoadBalancerAttributes | Updates persisted load balancer attributes. |\n| DescribeLoadBalancerAttributes | Returns attributes stored for a load balancer. |\n| DescribeCapacityReservation | Returns the stored capacity reservation fields for a load balancer. |\n| SetSecurityGroups | Replaces the security groups associated with a load balancer. |\n| SetSubnets | Replaces the subnets associated with a load balancer. |\n| SetIpAddressType | Updates the IP address type stored for a load balancer. |\n\n### Target Groups\n\n| Action | Description |\n|--------|-------------|\n| CreateTargetGroup | Creates a target group with protocol, port, health check, and target-type settings. |\n| DescribeTargetGroups | Lists or returns stored target groups. |\n| ModifyTargetGroup | Updates mutable target group settings. |\n| DeleteTargetGroup | Deletes an unused target group. |\n| ModifyTargetGroupAttributes | Updates persisted target group attributes. |\n| DescribeTargetGroupAttributes | Returns attributes stored for a target group. |\n\n### Targets\n\n| Action | Description |\n|--------|-------------|\n| RegisterTargets | Registers targets with a target group. |\n| DeregisterTargets | Removes targets from a target group. |\n| DescribeTargetHealth | Returns target health records maintained by Floci. |\n\n### Listeners\n\n| Action | Description |\n|--------|-------------|\n| CreateListener | Creates a listener and its non-deletable default rule. |\n| DescribeListeners | Lists or returns stored listeners. |\n| ModifyListener | Updates a listener's configuration and default actions. |\n| ModifyListenerAttributes | Updates persisted listener attributes. |\n| DescribeListenerAttributes | Returns attributes stored for a listener. |\n| DeleteListener | Deletes a listener and stops its socket. |\n| AddListenerCertificates | Adds certificates to a listener. |\n| RemoveListenerCertificates | Removes certificates from a listener. |\n| DescribeListenerCertificates | Lists certificates associated with a listener. |\n\n### Rules\n\n| Action | Description |\n|--------|-------------|\n| CreateRule | Creates a non-default listener rule with conditions, actions, and priority. |\n| DescribeRules | Lists or returns listener rules. |\n| ModifyRule | Updates a listener rule's conditions and actions. |\n| DeleteRule | Deletes a non-default listener rule. |\n| SetRulePriorities | Atomically updates rule priorities after validating uniqueness. |\n\n### Tags\n\n| Action | Description |\n|--------|-------------|\n| AddTags | Adds tags to supported ELBv2 resources. |\n| RemoveTags | Removes tags from supported ELBv2 resources. |\n| DescribeTags | Returns tags for supported ELBv2 resources. |\n\n### Metadata\n\n| Action | Description |\n|--------|-------------|\n| DescribeSSLPolicies | Returns Floci's pre-seeded standard SSL policy list. |\n| DescribeAccountLimits | Returns standard default ELBv2 account limits. |\n\n## Behavior Notes\n\n- Load balancer, target group, listener, rule, and tag state is persisted through Floci storage and rebuilt on service startup.\n- Load balancers are created in `active` state.\n- HTTP listener sockets are preserved when listener actions change and are restarted only when socket-level settings such as port change.\n- Instance targets are resolved through EC2 instance private addresses so local load balancer traffic can reach containers.\n- Target health starts in `initial` state with reason `Elb.RegistrationInProgress` and is updated by Floci's health checker when monitoring is active.\n- Health checks probe the target group's `HealthCheckPort` when it is a port number, and each target's own port when it is `traffic-port` (the default).\n- Each `CreateListener` automatically creates an immutable default rule (`priority=default`, `isDefault=true`). This rule cannot be deleted; use `ModifyListener` to change its action.\n- Rule priorities are unique per listener: `CreateRule` and `SetRulePriorities` only reject a priority held by another rule on the same listener. `SetRulePriorities` is atomic: all priority assignments are validated before any change is committed.\n- `DeleteTargetGroup` is rejected with `ResourceInUse` while the target group is referenced by any listener or rule.\n- `DeleteServerCertificate` is rejected with `DeleteConflict` while an IAM server certificate is named by a listener. Listener certificate ARNs are not validated when they are added.\n- `DeleteRule` is rejected with `OperationNotPermitted` for the default rule.\n- `DescribeSSLPolicies` returns a pre-seeded list of standard AWS SSL policies (`ELBSecurityPolicy-*`).\n- `DescribeAccountLimits` returns standard default limits (e.g., 50 load balancers per region, 100 target groups, etc.).\n- `routing.http.preserve_host_header.enabled` (default `false`) controls whether the original client Host header is forwarded to targets unchanged, or replaced with the target's `host:port`.\n- `RegisterTargets` rejects link-local and cloud instance-metadata addresses (`169.254.0.0/16`, `fe80::/10`, `fd00:ec2::254`) with `InvalidTarget`, and the load balancer and its health checks refuse to connect to them. Loopback and private addresses stay reachable so a load balancer can front a neighbouring container.\n\n## ARN Format\n\n```\narn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:{region}:{account-id}:loadbalancer/app/{name}/{hex16}\narn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:{region}:{account-id}:targetgroup/{name}/{hex16}\narn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:{region}:{account-id}:listener/app/{lb-name}/{lb-id}/{hex16}\narn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:{region}:{account-id}:listener-rule/app/{lb-name}/{lb-id}/{listener-id}/{hex16}\n```\n\n## Examples\n\n```bash\nexport AWS_ENDPOINT_URL=http://localhost:4566\n\n# Create a load balancer\naws elbv2 create-load-balancer \\\n  --name my-alb \\\n  --type application \\\n  --scheme internet-facing\n\n# Create a target group\naws elbv2 create-target-group \\\n  --name my-targets \\\n  --protocol HTTP \\\n  --port 80 \\\n  --target-type instance\n\n# Register targets\naws elbv2 register-targets \\\n  --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-east-1:000000000000:targetgroup/my-targets/abc123 \\\n  --targets Id=i-00000000001,Port=8080\n\n# Create a listener with a default forward action\naws elbv2 create-listener \\\n  --load-balancer-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-east-1:000000000000:loadbalancer/app/my-alb/abc123 \\\n  --protocol HTTP \\\n  --port 80 \\\n  --default-actions Type=forward,TargetGroupArn=arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-east-1:000000000000:targetgroup/my-targets/abc123\n\n# Add a path-based routing rule\naws elbv2 create-rule \\\n  --listener-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-east-1:000000000000:listener/app/my-alb/abc123/def456 \\\n  --priority 10 \\\n  --conditions Field=path-pattern,Values='/api/*' \\\n  --actions Type=forward,TargetGroupArn=arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-east-1:000000000000:targetgroup/my-targets/abc123\n\n# Describe load balancers\naws elbv2 describe-load-balancers\n\n# Describe target health\naws elbv2 describe-target-health \\\n  --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-east-1:000000000000:targetgroup/my-targets/abc123\n\n# Tag a resource\naws elbv2 add-tags \\\n  --resource-arns arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-east-1:000000000000:loadbalancer/app/my-alb/abc123 \\\n  --tags Key=env,Value=dev\n\n# Clean up\naws elbv2 delete-listener \\\n  --listener-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-east-1:000000000000:listener/app/my-alb/abc123/def456\naws elbv2 delete-load-balancer \\\n  --load-balancer-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-east-1:000000000000:loadbalancer/app/my-alb/abc123\naws elbv2 delete-target-group \\\n  --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-east-1:000000000000:targetgroup/my-targets/abc123\n```\n\n## Configuration\n\n| Environment variable | Default | Description |\n|---|---|---|\n| `FLOCI_SERVICES_ELBV2_ENABLED` | `true` | Enable or disable the ELBv2 service |\n\n## Listener Ports\n\nListener sockets bind on the Floci host. Expose any listener ports you need in Docker Compose when Floci itself runs in a container, similar to RDS and ElastiCache proxy ports.\n\n### Two load balancers on the same port\n\nIn AWS each load balancer has its own DNS name and addresses, so two of them can both listen on\nport 80 and never interact: the network picks the load balancer, and a `host-header` rule only picks\na rule inside one listener. Floci serves every load balancer from a single socket per port, so the\nHost header has to carry both decisions. A template that puts a public and an internal load balancer\non port 80 is correct for AWS and stays accepted here, but the request has to name the one it wants.\n\nA listener is chosen in this order:\n\n1. The Host header equals a load balancer's own DNS name (`{name}-{id}.elb.localhost.floci.io`).\n2. Exactly one listener on the port has a rule whose `host-header` condition matches the Host\n   header. This uses the same matching as the rule evaluation that follows, so it is\n   case-insensitive, ignores the port, and applies AWS's wildcards: `*` matches 0 or more\n   characters and `?` matches exactly 1, which means `*.example.com` claims `test.example.com`\n   but not `example.com`. `HostHeaderConfig.RegexValues` is not supported, by rule evaluation or\n   by selection, so a load balancer that names itself only through a regex cannot be selected\n   this way.\n3. Only one listener is on the port, in which case it answers any Host header.\n\nIf none of those resolve, and in particular when two load balancers declare the same hostname or\nneither declares any, the request answers `502 No listener for host`. Floci logs a warning naming\nboth load balancers the first time a second one takes a port, because the targets behind them stay\nhealthy and nothing else reports the collision.\n\nGiving each load balancer a `host-header` rule for the hostname it serves is usually enough, and it\nis the same configuration AWS needs. Moving one load balancer to a different listener port also\nworks, at the cost of a Floci-only difference from the deployed template.\n","metadata":{"truncated":false},"title":"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/floci-io/floci/main/docs/services/elb.md (text/plain; charset=utf-8)","time":{"start":1791610496654,"end":1791610496854}},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"caller":{"type":"direct"}}},"id":"prt_1244ea689001dk2kH5lB7DdII3","sessionID":"ses_edbb2023cffe1dP6YX8VsPdUc9","messageID":"msg_1244ea0b1001O2yDKa4fARuGeT"}}
